additional_requirements: The binge eating and inappropriate compensatory behaviors both occur, on average, at least once a week for 3 months

S045.name: Fear_of_Weight_Gain
S045.description: Intense fear of gaining weight or of becoming fat, even though at a significantly low weight.

subtypes.Fear of Weight Gain: Extreme fear and loathing of gaining weight or becoming fat.
subtypes.Fear of Specific Foods: Fear that eating high-calorie foods will immediately lead to weight gain.
subtypes.Obsession with Weight Gain: Compulsively checking the scale and becoming extremely anxious about even the slightest increase.

S046.name: Body_Image_Weight_Shape_Disturbance
S046.description: Undue influence of body weight or shape on self-evaluation.

subtypes.Distorted Body Image: Perceiving one's body as much fatter than it actually is or perceiving specific parts as excessively large when looking in the mirror.
subtypes.Self-Worth Dependent on Weight: Judging whether one is a good or successful person solely based on weight or body shape.

S048.name: Compensatory_Behavior_Purging
S048.description: Recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors involving the expulsion of food or fluids to prevent weight gain.

subtypes.Self-Induced Vomiting: Intentionally inducing vomiting to remove ingested food.
subtypes.Misuse of Medications: Repetitively misusing laxatives, diuretics, or enemas for the purpose of weight control.

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
examples: Eating more than 3-4 times the amount of a typical meal within 2 hours.
Continuously eating large amounts of high-calorie snacks in addition to main meals.
Eating enough to empty a significant portion of the refrigerator or pantry at once.
Eating clearly more food than others during the same period of time.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
examples: A feeling that once I start eating, I cannot stop even if I want to.
Thinking 'I shouldn't eat any more' but mechanically continuing to eat.
A feeling of helplessness that I cannot decide for myself how much to eat.
Eating as if my body is being controlled by someone else.

symptom.disease_info: Bulimia nervosa is characterized by recurrent binge-eating episodes with loss of control, followed by inappropriate compensatory behaviors, with self-evaluation strongly tied to body weight or shape and an intense fear of weight gain. It often develops gradually around dieting, stress, or appearance-related pressures and may remain hidden for months; it is distinguished from binge-eating disorder by compensatory behaviors and from anorexia nervosa by not being defined primarily by persistently low body weight.

patient.stressor_event: Major change in living condition (new home, remodeling, deterioration of neighborhood or home)
patient.stressor: After separating from his spouse, Agustín moved from their shared Evergreen Park home into a smaller apartment near the wildlife rescue center, where his routines around cooking, soccer, and late-night guitar sessions became less anchored. At first he tried to keep tight control over meals and exercise as a way to feel composed during the transition, but over the next five months his fear of weight gain and harsh self-judgment about his shape grew alongside episodes of eating unusually large amounts when alone after evening shifts. He began purging afterward to undo what he felt he had lost control over, keeping it hidden beneath his organized work persona and community commitments. He finally sought psychiatric care after a bilingual outreach presentation went poorly because he was preoccupied with when he could leave and compensate for what he had eaten earlier, prompting him to contact an employee assistance referral himself.

S045.name: Fear_of_Weight_Gain
S045.description: Intense fear of gaining weight or of becoming fat, even though at a significantly low weight.
S045.manifestation: If the scale is even a pound higher after a shift or my work pants feel tighter, I spend the whole day worrying I'm letting myself get fat and I start planning how to make up for it.

S046.name: Body_Image_Weight_Shape_Disturbance
S046.description: Undue influence of body weight or shape on self-evaluation.
S046.manifestation: When I look in the bathroom mirror at my apartment, all I can focus on is my stomach and waist, and if they look wrong I feel like I've failed at being disciplined, no matter how well I did at the rescue center that day.

S048.name: Compensatory_Behavior_Purging
S048.description: Recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors involving the expulsion of food or fluids to prevent weight gain.
S048.manifestation: After I eat like that, I usually end up in the bathroom making myself throw up because it feels like the only way to undo it before the calories settle in.

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
S049.manifestation: On nights after late shifts, I've eaten things like a full frozen pizza, cereal straight from the box, leftovers, and whatever snacks are in the cabinet within an hour or two, way more than I'd ever eat in front of anyone.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
S050.manifestation: I came in because once I start eating alone at night, it feels like something takes over and I can't stop, even while I'm telling myself to put the food away.

add_requirements.binge_eating_and_inappropriate_compensat: For at least the last four months, there has usually been at least one night each week where I eat far more than I meant to when I'm alone, and then I make myself throw up afterward.
add_requirements.functional_impairment: At work, I got so distracted during a bilingual outreach presentation thinking about leaving afterward that I stumbled through parts of it and worried my coworkers noticed.
add_requirements.duration: This has been going on for about five months, since I moved into the smaller apartment after separating from my spouse.
